title: Customer Onboarding Itinerary and Deployment Cadence
content:
Purpose:
Quick-run playbook for onboarding mid-market customers (example: ACME Corp) into a short POC that demonstrates latency and cost wins for our dedicated inference service. Designed to be readable by SEs, SREs, and the customer's infra lead.

Top-level goals:
- Turn up a reproducible demo integration in a 2-week sprint.
- Validate 95th percentile latency and per-token cost against customer workload sample.
- Produce an operational runbook + rollback plan that can be handed to customer ops.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- 2-week workshop + 4-week deployment cadence plan.
- Customer-verified acceptance criteria and basic perf metrics.
- Task tracker with owners and escape-hatch steps.
- Risk log and mitigation checklist.

Out-of-scope (for this POC):
- Full data residency / HSM on-prem implementation (can be follow-up).
- Model training or dataset curation services.

Key stakeholders:
- Customer: ACME Infra Lead: Jordan Hale (on-call during workshop)
- Redwood SE: Maya Li (owner), Samir Gupta (runtime integration)
- Redwood SRE: Elena Park (observability + infra playbacks)
- Solutions Eng PM: Ravi Menon (milestones, acceptance)
- Sales Sponsor: Priya Rao (contract & billing)

Prerequisites checklist (before Week 0 kickoff):
- Customer sample workload (1000 requests/day profile) uploaded to shared S3 link. (JIRA-9876)
- Customer provide temporary VPN/VPC peering details or allow public egress for demo.
- Demo account provisioned in Redwood Dedicated sandbox (env: acme-poc-01).
- Canary model artifacts (quantized variant) checked into repo branch.

Week-by-week cadence (high level):
- Week 0: Prep & alignment (3 business days)
  - Confirm sample dataset and SLA targets.
  - Create demo environment + baseline perf run (no caching).
  - Confirm access and logging hooks (tracing + token-level cost).

- Week 1: Workshop sprint (5 business days)
  - Day 1: Kickoff workshop (alignment, scope, roles) – 90m remote session.
  - Day 2: Integration lab – API wiring, auth, and small end-to-end request.
  - Day 3: Latency profiling + KV prefix caching demo.
  - Day 4: Batching & quantization experiment (measure cost).
  - Day 5: Acceptance rehearsal + runbook draft.

- Week 2: Harden & customer validation (5 business days)
  - Harden networking, add tracing tags for customer telemetry.
  - Run 3x load runs (low, medium, sim-prod) and collect metrics.
  - Customer validation session: review metrics, collect sign-off notes.

- Week 3–6: Optional scale-up (if customer commits)
  - Apply Dedicated sizing recommendations, configure autoscaling rules.
  - Canary rollout to small production slice and measure behavioral regressions.

Daily workshop itinerary (detailed for Week 1):
- Kickoff (Day 1) agenda:
  - 00:00–00:15 Welcome, goals, roles (Maya)
  - 00:15–00:35 Customer workload walkthrough (Jordan)
  - 00:35–00:55 Baseline perf & failure modes (Samir + Elena)
  - 00:55–01:30 Alignment on acceptance criteria + next steps

- Integration lab (Day 2) checklist (quick hits):
  - Ensure API key rotation policy is shared.
  - Verify client uses streaming versus non-streaming path as intended.
  - Attach tracing header and ensure it surfaces in Redwood Console.
  - Smoke test: full request cycle < 250ms median for simple query.

- Profiling day (Day 3) goals:
  - Show KV/prefix cache benefits on repeated queries.
  - Demonstrate trace waterfall and token breakdown in Console.
  - Capture 95th percentile and p99 with and without batching.

Acceptance criteria (must be signed by customer and SE):
- Functional: End-to-end request path exists, auth validated, retries handled.
- Performance: 95th percentile latency <= agreed target (example: 350ms) on a sim-prod run.
- Cost: Per-token cost reduction >= 20% vs baseline when applying recommended batching/caching.
- Observability: Traces, token-cost breakdown, and error-rate alerts present in Console.

Task tracker (working):
- Create demo env (acme-poc-01) — Owner: Maya Li — Status: done — Notes: sandbox provisioned 2026-01-22
- Baseline perf run (no caching) — Owner: Samir Gupta — Status: in_progress — Due: 2026-01-26
- Tracing hook + sample dashboard — Owner: Elena Park — Status: in_progress — Due: 2026-01-28
- Workshop slide deck + lab notes — Owner: Maya Li — Status: draft — Due: 2026-01-24
- Autoscale policy draft — Owner: Ravi Menon — Status: todo — Due: post-POC

Risk register (short):
- Customer network blocks outbound ports
  - Impact: High — Mitigation: use customer-provided bastion or ask for temporary egress. Plan B: upload request samples for remote replay.
- Sample workload not representative
  - Impact: Medium — Mitigation: collect additional traces; run sensitivity analysis across 3 distributions.
- Model variant mismatch (customer insists on custom weights)
  - Impact: Medium — Mitigation: agree to evaluate on provided artifact but hold off on SLA promises until perf baseline.

Escalation / escape hatch playbook:
- If latency > target after Week 1 experiments: revert to a smaller token window, enable stricter batching rules, and open SE-SRE war room.
- If customer infrastructure blocks connectivity: pivot to offline replay with recorded traces and provide a recorded demo.

Notes to self / rough ideas (scratch):
- Try pre-configuring a small local proxy that simulates KV cache for customer devs. Might reduce friction if they cannot accept dedicated edges during POC.
- Capture a one-pager comparing quantization profiles we tried and the tradeoffs — useful for postmortem.

Post-POC deliverables (if passed):
- Runbook + rollback checklist (PDF delivered to customer)
plain_text_preview: 2-week POC playbook to onboard ACME: kickoff workshop, integration lab, profiling, validation. Task tracker + risk register + acceptance criteria included. Owner: Maya Li.
